statement: Pens are sold only in packs of 2. Jo needs 9 pens. What is the smallest number of packs she must buy?

choices.misconception: I put 9 pens into twos, got 4 packs, and forgot about the 1 pen left over.
I thought Jo needs one pack for every pen.
I counted the pens Jo ends up with, not the packs.
I multiplied 9 by 2 instead of sharing 9 into twos.

hints: Can 9 be split exactly into twos?
9 is odd, so packs of 2 can never give exactly 9. Find how many packs give 8, then decide what to do about the last pen.
4 packs give 8 pens. Jo still needs 1 more pen, and pens only come in packs.

solutions.reliable: 4 packs give 8 pens, which is 1 too few. One more pack is needed for the ninth pen, so Jo buys 5 packs and has 1 pen spare. The idea to keep: an odd number cannot be split into twos, so there is always one left over, and it still needs a pack.
solutions.elegant: 10 is the first even number that is at least 9, and 10 pens make 5 packs. The idea to keep: when things come in twos, jump up to the next even number.

whyOnTest: Odd and even: 9 is odd, so pairs never fit it exactly, and forgetting the leftover pen is the trap.
